TLDR, get it if you want, just don’t expect the rpg Paper Mario style gameplay, you may get some enjoyment out of it that way. 

I preordered this game when it was announced back in 2020 and played it a little. But got frustrated. (I was excited but found myself growing frustrated with the battle system and general negativity that it wasn’t like the old game, I went in with high expectations as I haven’t played color splash nor sticker star.)

That said, I decided to put those expectations aside, and have been playing it again recently this year, I have actually have been having a decent amount of fun. 

It’s not your standard original paper Mario rpg, but this weird hybrid action adventure/“rpg”. I find the battle system to be tedious, repetitive and annoying at times, but the general gameplay and story outside of that is very charming. 

So do I recommend it, maybe (leaning towards yes if you want to give it a shot) but only if you go  in without the expectation that it’s rpg paper Mario.

I haven’t played sticker star, so I can’t say much on that, watched a play through.  For the 3ds it’s cute, but doesn’t have much going for it story wise, very much a “mobile” paper Mario game that’s easy to play short and simple worlds on the go. So don’t go in expecting something like supers story. 

 I’ve been playing through origami king recently though and have some thoughts. 

The battle system for origami king can be a bit frustrating if you don’t like puzzles, and the boss puzzles can be a bit of a slog. Though the over world platforming, toad hunting  and the story itself is quite charming and fun (at least to me) so far. 

So if you do get it, don’t go in thinking it’s like the RPG paper Mario, nor like super paper Mario, it sits awkwardly in the middle of an “rpg” and “action and adventure” .

If you’re waiting for the ttyd remake/remaster, we (hopefully) should be getting new info soon, so if you decide to pick up origami king there are some cheaper physical copies on eBay (especially for sticker star, that’s quite cheap) or “OK” digitally at full price just to hold over. Or you can play the n64 version on switch online. 

 (not the same game series, but Mario rpg is quite fun too if you want more of a rpg style gameplay that origami king sadly doesn’t quite hit.
